svg.title: The six layers of a context window, grouped by lifetime
svg.desc: A vertical stack of six layer cards, hand-drawn. From the top: system prompt, tools and MCP schemas, memory and state, retrieved RAG chunks, conversation history, and the user instruction. Each card names the layer's purpose and an illustrative token size. Brackets down the left group the layers by lifetime rather than by number: layers 01 and 02 form a stable prefix that caches, 03 and 04 are a per-turn injection and the biggest cost lever, 05 is a growing tail that runs out of room first, and 06 is the small trigger placed last. Down the right, one bar per layer shows effective attention across the window: longest beside the user instruction and the system prompt at the two ends, shortest beside the retrieved chunks in the middle, which is the lost-in-the-middle effect after Liu and colleagues, 2023.
svg.text: The six layers of a context window
One flat sequence of tokens, assembled from six parts with six different lifetimes.
JSON schema of every callable function
Sent in the order shown: 01 first, the user instruction last. Layers 01–02 are the stable prefix that caches;
03–04 are assembled fresh every turn; 05 grows without bound; 06 is small, last, and the reason for the rest.
